land.text: 'at the death of Zenodorus, Augustus gave Iturea to Herod the Great': the Iturean base and Zenodorus's Ulatha and Paneas

successors.note: Year inferred: Zenodorus ruled 23-20 BCE (Zenodorus son of Lysanias page); the Ituraea page says 'Three years later' than about 23 BC. The page does not say that Herod received the whole base: it says only 'Augustus gave Iturea to Herod the Great'. Iturea was later given again by Caligula to Soemus in 38 (annexed to Syria on his death, 49): not covered by this dossier.

capitals.name: Chalcis ad Libanum
capitals.note: The Ituraea page: 'with its centre in Chalcis ad Libanum' (it does not use 'capital'); the Itureans page has 'residence was at Chalcis(?)'. The coordinate is the usual site (Anjar / Majdal Anjar, in the Beqaa) and is not on the pages; the site is disputed.

correction.text: the Iturean base (Mount Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley, with the Anti-Lebanon slopes on the Syrian side, centred on Chalcis ad Libanum) with the Galilee that Aristobulus I then took (the judea dossier's reading)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The Itureans page puts the base 'around Mount Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley'; the Ituraea page extends it 'to the Anti-Lebanon Mountains in Syria'. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the whole country of Lebanon, which took in the Phoenician coastal cities of Tyre, Sidon and Berytus, is replaced by the Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates (Tyre and Sidon lie in South Lebanon, Berytus in Beirut, both outside; Byblos and Botrys on the Mount Lebanon coast are not carved out) plus a 25 km circle on the Syrian Anti-Lebanon, 25 cells, about 6,300 km2, against 35 cells (8,850 km2) before; the gazetteer has no Anti-Lebanon.] Galilee (17 cells, about 4,300 km2) is the zone of the judea dossier's /ledger/9 gain from this slug. The pages disagree on it: the Aristobulus I page says 'Most scholars assume the Ituraean territory to be northern Galilee'; the Itureans page puts the Iturean kingdom north of Galilee and says Upper and Lower Galilee 'appear to have remained outside Hasmonean borders'. Galilee is therefore the least certain part of the shape. No page gives an area.

correction.text: 'from Mount Lebanon across the plain of Marsyas to the Anti-Lebanon Mountains in Syria, with its centre in Chalcis ad Libanum': Mount Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley, with the Anti-Lebanon slopes on the Syrian side, centred on Chalcis ad Libanum

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the realm of Ptolemy son of Mennaeus (reign 85-40) and of his son Lysanias, 'from Mount Lebanon across the plain of Marsyas to the Anti-Lebanon Mountains in Syria' (Ituraea page). [Fix pass 2026-10-19: Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates plus an Anti-Lebanon circle in place of the whole country of Lebanon; about 6,300 km2.] No page gives a boundary or an area; the Roman province of Syria (64 BC) is not subtracted because the pages do not draw the frontier.

correction.text: the Iturean base (Mount Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley, with the Anti-Lebanon slopes on the Syrian side, centred on Chalcis ad Libanum) with 'areas south of Damascus (Ulatha and Paneas, both ... west of Trachonitis)' held by Zenodorus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the base plus the land Zenodorus held 'on lease we are told' from his father's territory: 'Josephus only gives us information concerning areas south of Damascus', Ulatha and Paneas, 'west of Trachonitis' (Zenodorus page; the lease 'may in fact' go back to 36 BCE, his rule is dated 23-20). [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the gazetteer's 'Damascus (region)' stand-in, an 80 km circle round Damascus itself (72 cells, about 18,200 km2), contradicted 'south of Damascus' and tripled the area; it is replaced by a 20 km circle at 35.69 E 33.15 N (Banias is not in the gazetteer), 4 cells, about 1,000 km2, the Huleh valley and Paneas; total 29 cells, about 7,300 km2.] Not drawn: 'the adjacent provinces' of the Ituraea page, which the Zenodorus page names as Trachonitis and Auranitis (taken from him and given to Herod; the Herod the Great page dates the grant 22 BCE and names no previous holder). No page gives an area.

region.text: the Iturean lands of Mount Lebanon, the Beqaa and the Anti-Lebanon slopes, with the Galilee that Aristobulus I campaigned for (the judea dossier's reading)

ledger.note: 105 BCE: the earliest date on the pages for the Iturean principality. Page silent on its origin: 'They first rose to power in the aftermath of the decline of the Seleucids in the 2nd century BC' (Itureans); the first dated sentence is 'In 105 BCE, Hasmonean leader Aristobulus I campaigned against Iturea'. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the base is the Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates plus an Anti-Lebanon circle, not the whole country of Lebanon (Ituraea page: 'It extended from Mount Lebanon across the plain of Marsyas to the Anti-Lebanon Mountains in Syria'; Itureans page: 'their base around Mount Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley'); Galilee is added because the contest of 105 and the loss of 103 are fought over it, with the pages' disagreement on it set out in the first keyframe.]

region.text: Galilee, the ground the Hasmoneans took

ledger.note: 105 BCE: Aristobulus I attacks the Itureans. 'In 105 BCE, Hasmonean leader Aristobulus I campaigned against Iturea'; the zone (Galilee) is the judea dossier's reading of Josephus-based accounts, not the Ituraea page's. The Aristobulus I page: 'Aristobulus went to war against the Ituraeans and took territory from them', the place unknown, 'Most scholars assume the Ituraean territory to be northern Galilee'.

103 BCE: the campaign ends with the Hasmonean royal title (judea dossier: 'Aristobulus I takes the royal title and conquers Galilee', 104-103). Page silent on the end of this fighting. The Aristobulus I page has his reign 104-103 BCE ('until his death the next year, 103 BCE'), a year later than the 105 of the Ituraea page.

103 BCE: Galilee passes to the Hasmoneans. Page silent on the year: the Ituraea page gives the 105 campaign only and says Aristobulus 'added a large portion of it to the kingdom of Judea'; the Itureans page does not name Galilee as taken; the loss mirrors the judea dossier's gain from this slug (/ledger/9, confidence 2). The Aristobulus I page reads the land taken as northern Galilee.

36 BCE: the dynasty of Ptolemy son of Mennaeus (85-40) and Lysanias ends with Lysanias's execution and Zenodorus holds on a lease. The Zenodorus page: he 'may in fact have held the lease on his territories as far back as the time of his father's execution (36 BCE)', 'initially paying rent to Cleopatra'. The lessor was Cleopatra, then (page silent) Rome.

region.text: areas south of Damascus, Ulatha and Paneas, west of Trachonitis

ledger.note: 36 BCE: Zenodorus holds Ulatha and Paneas on lease from Cleopatra. 'He gained control, on lease we are told, of some of his father's territory', 'initially paying rent to Cleopatra' (Josephus only); 'Josephus only gives us information concerning areas south of Damascus', Ulatha and Paneas 'west of Trachonitis'. The page hedges the year ('may in fact have held the lease ... as far back as the time of his father's execution (36 BCE)'), hence confidence 1. The counterpart is the lessor, Cleopatra's Egypt: ptolemaic-kingdom /ledger/69 holds Coele-Syria from 34 and has no matching loss. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: replaces the 23 BCE gain of the gazetteer's 'Damascus (region)' from 'nobody'.]

23 BCE: Zenodorus's principality. 'About 23 BC, Iturea with the adjacent provinces fell into the hands of a chief named Zenodorus' (Ituraea page); the Zenodorus page dates his rule 23-20 BCE, 'the ruler of a small principality in the vicinity of Damascus'. This is a change of ruler, not a dated gain from nobody: the lease may reach back to 36 BCE (previous event) and the page names no earlier holder of the 'adjacent provinces' (Trachonitis and Auranitis on the Zenodorus page, not drawn here). [Fix pass 2026-10-19: was a gain of the Damascus region from 'nobody'.]

region.text: Iturea with the adjacent provinces: the Iturean base and Zenodorus's Ulatha and Paneas

ledger.note: 20 BCE: Augustus gives Iturea to Herod the Great. 'Three years later, at the death of Zenodorus, Augustus gave Iturea to Herod the Great' (the page gives no year; 23 + 3 = 20). The Zenodorus page says Augustus gave Trachonitis to Herod and 'confiscated' Auranitis, no year; the Herod the Great page dates the grant of Trachonitis, Batanaea and Auranitis to 22 BCE and says nothing of Zenodorus, Ulatha or Iturea's gift. The judea dossier has no event in 20 (its /ledger/32 is the 22 grant of Hauran from roman-empire).

region.text: Iturea with the adjacent provinces: the Iturean base and Zenodorus's Ulatha and Paneas

ledger.note: 20 BCE: the Iturean principality ends with Zenodorus, who 'died soon afterwards in Antioch'; Herod the Great receives the land.

wars.name: Aristobulus I's campaign against Iturea
wars.outcome: 'In 105 BCE, Hasmonean leader Aristobulus I campaigned against Iturea'; the judea dossier has Galilee conquered by 103. The Aristobulus I page: he 'took territory from them', probably northern Galilee, reign 104-103.
wars.note: The Itureans page also dates the campaign 105 BCE; the judea dossier uses 104-103 for the royal title. Sources for the zone disagree (see the first keyframe).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the Iturean principality; the Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates, a circle on the Anti-Lebanon and (from 36) a circle at Ulatha and Paneas stand in.

sources.title: Itureans
sources.note: Rise after the Seleucid decline, 105 BCE Aristobulus, Ptolemy 85-40, Zenodorus c. 23, Herod, Soemus 38-49.

sources.title: Ituraea
sources.note: The same dated sentences; extent from Mount Lebanon to the Anti-Lebanon, centre at Chalcis ad Libanum.

sources.title: Zenodorus son of Lysanias
sources.note: Rule 23-20 BCE near Damascus; lease from Cleopatra from 36; Trachonitis and Auranitis to Herod.

sources.title: Aristobulus I
sources.note: Reign 104-103 BCE; 'went to war against the Ituraeans and took territory from them'; most scholars read it as northern Galilee.

sources.title: Herod the Great
sources.note: 22 BCE: Augustus grants Herod Trachonitis, Batanaea and Auranitis; names no previous holder, no Zenodorus.

notes:
Three pages (budget 2-5). The pages are thin: no Iturean origin, no Ptolemy-son-of-Mennaeus territory, no Lysanias dates (his execution in 36 is on the Zenodorus page only as 'his father's execution (36 BCE)'). Pages tried and failed: Ptolemy son of Mennaeus, Lysanias of Abilene (not found); Chalcis ad Libanum is the town of Anjar (a different article). The Soemus kingdom (38-49) and the later Chalcis kingdoms of Herod of Chalcis and Agrippa II are not covered; a gap-filler should open 'Chalcis (kingdom)' or 'Herod of Chalcis'. The Galilee event is the judea dossier's reading (counterpart itureans). Capital coordinates are the usual site, not from the pages. Gazetteer names wanted: Iturea, Chalcis ad Libanum, Ulatha, Paneas, Anti-Lebanon.

Fix pass 2026-10-19 (after review-me-05-x, verdict fail). Five pages now (budget 2-5): Aristobulus I and Herod the Great were opened for the repair; all were opened again by WebFetch for the date, region and source questions below. (1) Base: the whole country of Lebanon is replaced by the Beqaa and Mount Lebanon governorates plus a 25 km circle at 36.3 E 33.85 N for the Syrian Anti-Lebanon (the gazetteer has no Anti-Lebanon; a gazetteer entry should replace the circle); Byblos and Botrys on the Mount Lebanon coast are inside the governorate and are not carved out. (2) Galilee: kept in the found region and the first keyframe, because the judea dossier's /ledger/9 gain (counterpart itureans) and this dossier's contest and loss are fought over it. Disagreement: the Aristobulus I page says 'Most scholars assume the Ituraean territory to be northern Galilee', the Itureans page puts Iturea north of Galilee and says the Galilees 'appear to have remained outside Hasmonean borders'; judea draws all of Galilee (17 cells), the pages support at most its north, so me-05-f may wish to narrow it. (3) Zenodorus: the Damascus stand-in (an 80 km circle round Damascus itself, 18,200 km2) contradicted the Zenodorus page ('areas south of Damascus', Ulatha and Paneas 'west of Trachonitis') and is replaced by a 20 km circle at 35.69 E 33.15 N (about 1,000 km2); the 23 BCE gain from 'nobody' is a rename (the Ituraea page's 'fell into the hands of' is a change of ruler), and the land comes in at 36 BCE as a gain from the lessor, Cleopatra's Egypt (ptolemaic-kingdom), at confidence 1 because the page hedges the lease's year. I disagree with one part of the reviewer's reading: the Ituraea page's 23 BC sentence also says 'with the adjacent provinces', which the Zenodorus page names as Trachonitis and Auranitis, so Zenodorus's principality was larger than the circle in 23-22; I did not draw them because no page dates when he acquired them, and the Herod the Great page (22 BCE) names no previous holder, so the judea dossier's /ledger/32 (gain of Hauran from roman-empire) stands unmatched here; me-05-f should decide whether its counterpart is itureans. Still thin (not opened, page budget spent): the origin and founding year of the Iturean principality (Herod of Chalcis page suggested), Pompey's settlement of 64-63 BC and the Roman client status 63-20 (Third Mithridatic War page suggested; neither the Itureans nor the Ituraea page mentions Pompey, so no vassal events are written), the Parthian-era and Cleopatra years 40-30. Mirrors: the 36 gain names ptolemaic-kingdom (me-05-b), which has Coele-Syria from 34 and no loss; the 20 loss names judea, whose ledger has no event in 20.
